label: the independent vowel letters, used word-initially
note: A, AA, U, UU, E and I were taught as independents and II, O, AI and AU were not, so a candidate could not begin a word with any of the four. Chapter 65 closes it, one short lesson per letter. THE POINT IS STILL SEPARATE FROM MR-A1-OR-14, which is the ai and au SIGNS and closed at chapters 56 and 59: a sign hangs on a consonant, a letter starts a word, and the two shapes look nothing alike. All four of these letters had a sign the reader already drew -- ii and o since chapter one -- so the gap was never in the sound but in the POSITION, which is what made it easy to miss. It was also blocking a number in the middle of an ordinary counting sequence: ऐंशी, eighty, opens with the independent AI.
